name: Abkhaz
variety: Literary Abkhaz, based on the Abzhywa dialect (58 consonants). The Bzyp dialect has 67 consonants and Sadz 60; the Cwyzhy variety described in the Journal of the IPA is spoken in Turkey.
sources: Hewitt, B. George (1979). Abkhaz. Lingua Descriptive Studies 2. Amsterdam: North-Holland.
Hewitt, George (2010). Abkhaz: A Comprehensive Self-Tutor. Munich: Lincom Europa.
Chirikba, Viacheslav A. (2003). Abkhaz. Munich: Lincom Europa.
Spruit, Arie (1986). Abkhaz Studies. PhD dissertation, University of Leiden.
Catford, J. C. (1972). Labialization in Caucasian languages, with special reference to Abkhaz. Proceedings of the 7th International Congress of Phonetic Sciences.
Catford, J. C. (1977). Mountain of tongues: the languages of the Caucasus. Annual Review of Anthropology 6.
Andersson, Samuel, Vaux, Bert & Pysipa (Şener), Zihni (2023). Cwyzhy Abkhaz. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 53(1): 266-286.
Meurer, Paul (2011). A finite state approach to Abkhaz morphology and stress. In Logic, Language, and Computation (TbiLLC 2009), Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence. Springer.
Beguš, Gašper (2021). Segmental phonetics and phonology in Caucasian languages. In Maria Polinsky (ed.), The Oxford Handbook of Languages of the Caucasus. Oxford University Press.
contrasts: three-way laryngeal contrast in stops and affricates: voiced, voiceless aspirated, ejective
plain, palatalised and labialised series of velars and uvulars: kʰ kʲʰ kʷʰ, qʼ qʲʼ qʷʼ, χ χʲ χʷ, ʁ ʁʲ ʁʷ
labialised dental stops and labialised alveolo-palatal affricates: dʷ tʷʰ tʷʼ, dʑʷ tɕʷʰ tɕʷʼ
three places for sibilants: alveolar s z, palato-alveolar ʃ ʒ (with labialised ʃʷ ʒʷ), retroflex ʂ ʐ, and the matching affricates
uvular against pharyngeal fricatives: χ against ħ, χʷ against ħʷ
two vowels, open /a/ and close central /ə/ (a vertical system); long /aː/ is a third vowel or a sequence /aa/
allophony: /a/ is [e] next to /j/ and palatalised consonants and [o] next to /w/ and labialised consonants; /ə/ is [i] and [u] in the same surroundings
the letters е, о, и, у stand for these coloured vowels or for the sequences /aj/, /aw/ (or /wa/), /jə/ (or /əj/), /wə/ (or /əw/); и and у before a vowel are the glides /j/ and /w/
unstressed /ə/ is dropped unless the result would be a cluster of three or more consonants; a /ə/ with secondary stress is kept (Spruit 1986)
the labialised dental stops have full lip closure with the tongue closure: /dʷ tʷʰ tʷʼ/ are [d͡b t͡pʰ t͡pʼ]

labialisation of the alveolo-palatal affricates is labiodental; of /ʃʷ ʒʷ ħʷ/ it is of the [ɥ] type (rounding with a raised tongue front); of velars and uvulars it is plain rounding [w] (Catford 1972)
aspiration and ejection are both weak unless the speaker is emphatic
/qʼ/ is a uvular ejective stop, often affricated; between vowels it may be a glottal stop
/ɥ/ comes from an older voiced pharyngeal with rounding and keeps a pharyngeal colouring for some speakers
/r/ is an alveolar trill or tap
syllable_structure: underlying CV with /a/ or /ə/; after schwa deletion the surface allows (C)(C)V(C)(C)
phonotactics: every syllable has the shape consonant plus /a/ or /ə/ at the underlying level (Spruit 1986)
loss of unstressed /ə/ creates clusters of two consonants at the beginning and end of words
clusters of three or more consonants are broken up by /ə/
most nouns are cited with the article prefix a-
the vowels [e i o u] do not contrast with /a ə/ plus glide in native words

stress.rule: Every syllable of every morpheme is lexically accented (dominant) or unaccented (recessive); stress falls on the first accented syllable that is not directly followed by another accented syllable, other such syllables get secondary stress, and a word without any such syllable is stressed on its last syllable (Dybo's rule in the form given by Spruit 1986).
stress.cues: intensity and pitch; the stressed syllable keeps its /ə/ while unstressed /ə/ is deleted, so the presence of the vowel is itself a cue. No instrumental study is cited.

rhythm.vowel_reduction: strong: unstressed /ə/ is deleted; /a/ keeps its quality
rhythm.notes: The class is an impressionistic label based on schwa deletion and the consonant clusters it creates; no rhythm-metric study is cited.

length.notes: Long /aː/ (written аа) contrasts with /a/. Geminate consonants arise across morpheme boundaries in the literary language and are contrastive in the Sadz and Cwyzhy varieties. No duration measurements are cited.

intonation.declarative: falling contour over the sentence; the verb is final
intonation.yes_no_question: marked on the verb by a suffix (-ma and others), with raised pitch on the verb
intonation.wh_question: marked by question affixes inside the verb or by a question word; prominence on the questioned element
intonation.continuation: non-final clauses end on sustained or rising pitch
intonation.notes: No instrumental description of Abkhaz intonation was available; these settings are provisional. Questions are marked in the verb morphology, so intonation carries less of the load than in European languages (Hewitt 1979).

tone.notes: No lexical tone; the accent system is a stress system with lexically marked syllables.

phonation: ejective stops and affricates (glottalic egressive), weakly ejected in ordinary speech

problems: The ejectives п т к ҵ ҷ ҿ are plain unaspirated consonants (p_, t_ and k_ use consonants/p-, consonants/t- and ustop/k_unasp2); the ejc flag is set on some of them but no glottalic release is synthesised.

The uvular ejectives ҟ ҟь ҟә (q, qj, qw) are declared as voiced fricatives and built from the formants of the voiced uvular fricative (voc/Q_ulv), so they sound like a voiced fricative, not an ejective stop.
Several voiceless consonants are flagged voiced and built on voiced formant data: қ (kʰ), қә (kʷʰ), кә (kʷʼ), ҭә (tʷʰ), тә (tʷʼ), ч (tʃʰ) and ҷ (tʃʼ).
ҩ /ɥ/ is defined as a vowel (phoneme Uw), so it counts as a syllable and takes the stress: аҩны gives [aˈɥnə].
у and и are always the vowels [u] and [i]; the glides /w/ and /j/ are never produced: уара gives [uˈara] and аԥсуа gives [apsˈua].
аа, the long vowel /aː/, is two separate short vowels.
е, и, о, у are independent vowel phonemes of fixed quality; the colouring of /a ə/ by palatalised and labialised consonants is not modelled.

No stress rule is set for ab, so the default penultimate stress applies, which in words with the article a- is usually the article; Abkhaz stress is lexical and mobile. The deletion of unstressed schwa is absent.
The labialised dental stops дә тә ҭә have no lip closure, and labialisation in general is made by mixing in the sound of a vowel [u].
Vowel lengths are not set consistently (u has length 40, a and o have none), and the table 'ab' is declared twice in phsource/phonemes.
Some IPA names are missing, so p_ and t_ appear in IPA output.
good: every letter and digraph of the Abkhaz alphabet maps to its own phoneme, including the palatalised and labialised series
the voiced, aspirated and ejective series are kept apart as three sets of phonemes
pharyngeal ħ ħʷ and the uvular fricatives χ ʁ with their palatalised and labialised partners are present

notes: No formant or voice onset time figures are given because none could be checked for Abkhaz. For the related Ubykh, Beguš (2021) measured /a/ at F1 745 Hz, F2 1712 Hz and the close vowel at F1 424 Hz, F2 1958 Hz from one archive recording; similar values are proposed for Abkhaz but are not used here.
